newsitem.title: JORDAN: British jet car cruises at 320 mph in desert test.
newsitem.headline: British jet car cruises at 320 mph in desert test.

text.p: Britain's world land speed record challenger Thrust SSC made its second trial run in Jordan on Saturday, clocking 320 mph (512 kph), organisers said.

"We altered the suspension and the steering after the first run (on Tuesday)," said Andrew Noble, whose brother Richard is leading the Thrust team's attempt to break his own world record of 633.47 mph (1,019.44 kph) in Jordan.
The 9.5 tonne, 16 metre car's suspension is controlled by a computer-run "active ride suspension" -- processing information from 145 sensors on the car.
"The alterations were successful and we can now progress to higher speeds," Andrew Noble told Reuters.

He said the next scheduled run would be on Tuesday, when the team would take the car up to around 450 mph (720 kph). Once it breaks 500 mph the car will be completely overhauled, a process expected to take two days, before speeds are gradually ratcheted up towards the record.
The Thrust tests, in the Jafr desert about 200 km south of Amman, have been hampered by high winds, but Noble said the long-term weather forecast was in their favour.
If the runs in Jordan go to plan the Thrust team hope next year to take the car beyond the speed of sound, about 750 mph (1,200 kph) at sea level.
